title: WPSB/379/2013 of Shashank Pandey Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 379 of 2013
Shashank Pandey .......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ......Respondents.
Mr. Shashank Pandey, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Addl. Chief Standing Counsel for State/respondent no. 1.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Dated: 09.03.2016
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
The prayers in the writ petition are as follows:
 "a. To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus commanding the respondents to get the
answer sheet of the petitioner evaluated by the committee
of the members having expertise in the subject.
 b. To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus commanding to declare the petitioner
successful in the final absorption test held in the month
of December 2006 and the petitioner be treated as
absorbed in the job from the date since the other
candidates those passed the (2006) test were absorbed"
2. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
Petitioner was appointed as Assistant Engineer (Trainee) by
UJVN Limited. The Managing Director and the Director (H.R.)
respectively are shown as respondent nos. 2 & 3 in the writ petition.
Petitioner was appointed on probation for a period of one year. He
had to undergo a final absorption test. The said test was held in the
year 2006. The prayers made in the writ petition are in regard to the
said test.
3. A counter affidavit is filed, wherein the question of the writ
petition being highly belated is raised. It is pointed out inter alia that
the last representation, which was made by the petitioner, was in the

2
month of April, 2011 and it was rejected in the month of June, 2011.
Petitioner has also not stated as to what happened in between 2011
and 2013. Respondents have also given some reasons in regard to the
question raised on merits.
4. We have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the
learned counsel for respondent nos. 2 and 3.
5. We notice that the test was held in the year 2006. Apparently,
petitioner did know about the fate of his attempt in the test; but he
kept quiet. For the first time, he moves in the matter by applying
under the Right to Information Act in the year 2010. Armed with the
information, apparently, he moved a representation, which was
rejected in the year 2011. The same is produced as Annexure-12.
From the prayers, we notice that the petitioner has not chosen to
challenge the said decision. Moreover, we have also noticed that from
2006 to 2010, petitioner did not take any step in the matter. We would
think that, in the circumstances of the case, the writ petition is without
merit.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed. No order as to costs.
